Title: January 8, 2026 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting (with Downtown Commercial District, Nwood Metropolitan District, and annexation/ordinance hearings)
Overview: The council heard extensive open comment on Flock Safety cameras, PSPS outages, proportional representation, and other topics, then received a staff recap of the December wind and power shut-off response. It approved the consent agenda including the Sundance Institute governing agreement, approved Downtown Commercial District Resolution 319 for Sundance incentives, and passed the 915 Fifth Street annexation ordinances. It also amended and passed Ordinance 8721 on landscaping, water conservation, and wildfire resilience for a third reading, declined to call up an Arapahoe Avenue form-based code project, and discussed 2026 committee appointments.

Topic1.Title: Open Comment Period
Topic1.Summary: Residents spoke on a range of topics including surface parking at Engineering Center, Flock Safety camera vulnerabilities and data sharing, CU student move-out waste diversion, Eco Visits for wildlife, council decorum and Caterpillar divestment, proportional representation, Excel Energy and a sustainable energy utility, and rec center lap pool concerns. Staff and council responded briefly to the comments, including follow-ups on resilience hubs, closed captioning, and Flock data policy.

Topic2.Title: PSPS and Windstorm Response Summary
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented a recap of the city's response to the December public safety power shut-off and windstorm, including emergency operations center activation, increased fire and police call volume, and generator support for water plants and intersections. Around 60% of the community lost power, and no serious injuries or fires were reported. A virtual town hall and an after-action report are planned, and the city will work with Excel and the PUC on future shut-off planning. Council thanked staff for the response.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda and Sundance Institute Agreement
Topic3.Summary: The council approved the consent agenda items, with item 4D removed earlier, including the governing agreement with the Sundance Institute to host the Sundance Film Festival from 2027 through 2036. Staff explained the agreement includes parking revenue sharing and reporting terms. Council members raised concerns about community benefit tracking and the lack of an equity analysis, and the consent agenda passed unanimously.

Topic4.Title: Downtown Commercial District Board Actions
Topic4.Summary: The council convened as the Downtown Commercial District board and approved Resolution 319, which sets incentives for the Sundance Institute and authorizes the general manager to negotiate and execute a lease. A council member asked whether the parking revenue split depends on current or future rates, and staff confirmed it is based on festival-period pricing with a 50/50 split. The board then adjourned and reconvened as the city council.

Topic5.Title: Call-Up of Arapahoe Avenue Form-Based Code Review
Topic5.Summary: The council considered calling up a form-based code review for a five-story mixed-use building with 300 dwelling units at 5501 and 5505 Arapahoe Avenue. Some members said the form-based code produced a poor aesthetic result, but others stressed keeping the administrative track predictable and not punishing applicants who followed the rules. The motion to call up the project failed 4 to 5, so the project was not called up.

Topic6.Title: Nwood Metropolitan District Budget Amendment
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented a supplemental appropriation of about $7,400 for the 2025 Nwood Metropolitan District budget to cover dissolution-related expenses that exceeded the original budget, and noted an accounting error that created a negative fund balance. The public hearing drew comments from one resident about the cost. Council then adopted Resolution 4 unanimously and reconvened as the city council.

Topic7.Title: 915 Fifth Street Annexation and Zoning
Topic7.Summary: Council held the second reading on the series annexation of the 1.294-acre property at 915 Fifth Street, with initial RE zoning. Staff recommended against the planning board's proposed 4,000-square-foot floor area limit because it was inconsistent with past annexations, and the applicant did not want that restriction. Council adopted Resolution 1364, Resolution 1365, and Ordinances 8728, 8729, and 8730, and the water conservancy district consent, all unanimously.

Topic8.Title: Ordinance 8721: Landscaping, Water Conservation, and Wildfire Resilience
Topic8.Summary: Staff presented revisions to landscape code and wildland urban interface requirements, moving technical standards into a city manager landscape manual, updating non-functional turf rules to comply with state law, and clarifying wildfire hardening rules. Changes from earlier council feedback included removing tree removal requirements, restoring existing trigger thresholds, allowing daytime watering in winter, and easing weed barrier restrictions. Council amended and passed the ordinance, which will move to third reading.

Topic9.Title: 2026 Council Committee Appointments
Topic9.Summary: Staff walked council through vacancies on boards, committees, and sister city liaison roles, with members volunteering for Boulder County Consortium of Cities, Mile High Flood District, Boards and Commissions Committee, Charter Committee, Financial Strategy Committee, and intergovernmental affairs. Members also swapped sister city liaisons and Taisha offered to give up the Audit Committee seat. Council asked staff to look into moving the ARAB seat to staff and to clarify the county homelessness working group appointment, with a January 13 deadline for recommendations.
